A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HiRes-LLaVA, its SliceRestore Adapter, Self-Mining Sampler, and EntityGrid-QA benchmark. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support a reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, EntityGrid-QA results, component and kernel-size ablations, data-efficiency experiments, and qualitative outputs.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark evaluations and ablations, including additional comparisons controlling training data, separator experiments, and computational-efficiency measurements in the appendix.

M1.justification: The proposed training procedure changes from two-stage adapter/LoRA training with frozen base encoders and LLMs to three stages including full-model capability enhancement and subsequent LLM instruction tuning. The main model adopts InternViT and Llama-3.1. v2 also specifies SMS attention restricted to each pooled query's S×S source region, whereas v1 describes Cross-Attn(Pc,P) over the slice features.

E1.justification: EntityGrid-QA changes from identification, relative-position, and counting tasks to identification across four entity types. The main evaluation removes STVQA, LLaVA-W, POPE, and HallusionBench and adds MME and MM-Vet. Training coverage also expands through sources such as TextbookQA and IconQA; the appendix's V* and Image2HTML examples were already present in v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds comparisons with LLaVA-MORE and Cambrian-1, replaces mPLUG-Owl2 and mPLUG-DocOwl with newer generations, and removes comparators including InstructBLIP and Donut. EntityGrid-QA Table 2 adds LLaVA-1.5 and removes Monkey. The component ablation also gains a LLaVA baseline.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 replaces the 1.6M-pretraining/1.5M-instruction recipe with 558K alignment, 1.8M enhancement, and 3M instruction stages. Instruction batch size changes from 128 to 256, learning rates and adapter placement change, and InternViT introduces a nine-slice configuration alongside CLIP's sixteen slices. New experiments vary slice counts, backbones, and training-data controls; the discrepancy metric's sign also changes.

E4.justification: v2 adds a global-only SRA ablation, slice-count sensitivity, vision-encoder/LLM comparisons, matched-training-data controls, and shared-versus-distinct separator tests (Tables 3, 4, 6, 10, and 11). Appendix C adds component and model efficiency analyses. The earlier kernel-size and data-efficiency analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report accuracy means and standard deviations in Table 2, without seeds, repeated-training counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2 documents no new uncertainty-estimation procedure. Its retained reference to averaging across 'three tasks' leaves aggregation unclear for the revised benchmark.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the older HiRes configurations with new-model results, including DocVQA 84.9 versus v1's 74.7 for its 336px model, under different training and backbone settings. Retained comparator entries also change, such as TextMonkey+ ChartQA from 66.9 to 59.9. EntityGrid-QA results are replaced for the redesigned task, and new ablation and timing results appear. Kernel-size results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 Equation 5 defines Discrepancy2 as (edge accuracy minus center accuracy)/center accuracy; v2 Equation 6 reverses the numerator. This corrects a mathematical metric definition to match the reported positive edge-performance deficits, rather than merely renaming it.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain SRA, SMS, and a benchmark for fragmentation. The benchmark contribution is narrowed from identification, position, and counting to identification at different slice positions. The abstract and introduction also introduce a quantified approximately 12% superiority claim, while retaining the broader effectiveness and data-efficiency claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations attributing gains to the method through matched-data comparisons and defending synthetic EntityGrid-QA as sufficient for assessing fragmentation. Appendix D distinguishes its non-overlapping-slice problem from LLaVA-UHD's overlapping-slice counting problem. Meanwhile, v1's explicit limitation concerning simple backgrounds and restricted entity/task diversity disappears; the broader-impact cautions remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A and Tables 7–9 substantially expand dataset inventories and document per-stage trainable modules, token limits, learning rates, and epochs. Benchmark distractor generation and object sourcing become explicit. Tables 12–13 specify efficiency-measurement hardware and procedures. Conversely, v1's main-training statement of two days on 64 V100 GPUs under FP16 and its LoRA rank/alpha details are no longer supplied.

R1.justification: The related-work taxonomy and central fragmentation argument remain. v2 updates citations and comparisons to newer work, including Cambrian-1, DeCo, LLaVA-MORE, and newer mPLUG models, and adds an explicit distinction from LLaVA-UHD's benchmark. These refine the existing positioning rather than replacing it.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and benchmark description undergo substantial rewriting. Dynamic slicing moves into a new overall-framework subsection, related-work subsections are consolidated, and the appendix is reorganized into separate implementation, ablation, efficiency, discussion, visualization, and broader-impact sections. These are extensive narrative and structural changes.

P2.justification: The paper changes to a two-column layout. Figure 1 replaces positional heatmaps with fragmentation comparison bars, Figure 2 is extensively redrawn, and benchmark diagrams/examples are revised. Comparison tables are restructured and numerous analysis tables are added. Several qualitative figures and the data-efficiency figure retain their underlying content despite visual adjustments.

improvement.justification: The added matched-data controls, component analyses, resource measurements, and fuller training recipe strengthen empirical support and reproducibility beyond v1. The net gain is limited by the narrower EntityGrid-QA task coverage, removal of its explicit limitation, and reporting inconsistencies: Table 2 still refers to three tasks, while Appendix C claims a 74% training-time reduction although Table 12 implies about 84%. Higher main-table scores alone do not establish improvement because model and training settings changed.
